# Multi-Country Car Insurance — Technical Assessment

One Angular 21 application serves the Colombia and Chile quote wizard. Strapi 5 publishes each country's form configuration, plan catalog, and terms. The wizard covers details entry, plan selection, quote review, consent, and simulated payment. Quote and vehicle values use fictitious data and stay in the browser.

## Run the wizard

Use Docker with Compose and run the following command from the repository root.

```sh
docker compose up --build
```

Open [the country picker](http://localhost:8080). Both [Colombia](http://localhost:8080/co/quote/details) and [Chile](http://localhost:8080/cl/quote/details) support direct links. The first startup builds the app and publishes sample forms, plans, and terms for both countries into a Strapi SQLite volume. It generates Strapi secrets in that local volume. Restarts preserve later editorial changes.

The public wizard and the seeded forms, plans, and terms are available as soon as the stack is ready. An administrator account is optional for evaluating the wizard. To edit content, open [Strapi's loopback administration panel](http://localhost:1337/admin) and create the first local administrator using the registration form shown on a fresh volume. This is the local Strapi account and requires no Strapi Cloud account. Administrator credentials stay with the local Strapi instance. See the [Strapi first-run guide](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/quick-start).

In Content Manager, open **Quote form configuration**, edit fields within the existing form for the selected country, then publish the complete form. Reload the application or open the other country URL to fetch current content. Ordinary navigation within the same country's wizard reuses the ready configuration in memory.

In Content Manager, open **Quote plan** to edit a country's plans. Publish each plan and set it active to offer it. Enter base prices in major units with currency COP for Colombia (up to two fractional digits) or CLP for Chile (whole pesos). The published base price is the final price. Plans are read on entry to the plan step and checked again at the Summary handoff. The user must choose again if their plan was removed or repriced.

In Content Manager, open **Quote terms** and edit the existing Terms document for the country. Publish the document to make its multiline plain text available on Summary. Terms are checked again on Pay. If the published text has changed, the user must review and accept the updated terms before paying.

The demo-only outcome defaults to Approved. Select Rejected to test recovery, then select Approved and retry with the same quote. A successful simulation shows a quote number and masked read-only quote summary that survive reload in the same tab when browser storage is available. To clear the completed quote and return to Details for the same country, choose **Iniciar una nueva cotización**.

### Synchronize an existing local sample plan catalog

New databases already receive all three plans for each country. For the default local Compose volume created with the original two-plan catalog, build the current CMS image and preview the changes.

```sh
docker compose -p multi-country-car-insurance build cms
sh scripts/sync-dev-plans.sh --dry-run
```

The preview reads a consistent SQLite backup with the development volume mounted read-only. Review the proposed changes and copy the reported fingerprint when the status is `ready`. If the status is `blocked`, review the listed records in Strapi. A `noop` means the catalog is current.

```sh
docker compose -p multi-country-car-insurance stop web cms
sh scripts/sync-dev-plans.sh --apply FINGERPRINT
docker compose -p multi-country-car-insurance up -d
```

Replace `FINGERPRINT` with the value from the preview. Apply requires the stopped development volume and saves a database backup in that volume before writing. It recomputes the preview and checks both the draft and published versions in one transaction. Only exact original fixtures receive expanded benefits, and they retain their document IDs. The sync introduces Integral only when both country catalogs match the original fixtures and both Integral documents are absent. Conflicting edits, duplicates, unexpected or missing versions, and prior removal of a tracked Integral stop the whole update. The local administrator account and other content stay in the original volume.

If the owner approves preserving an existing Colombia Ruta price, add `--preserve-co-ruta-price PRICE` to both preview and apply. Use COP major units with two decimal places and no grouping separators. For example, use `--preserve-co-ruta-price 179900.00` for COP 179.900,00. Both stored versions must already have exactly that price. The sync preserves it and still checks every other field against the fixtures.

## Configuration and data boundaries

- The public app uses same-origin GET paths under `/api/quote-content/v1/:country/` for `form`, `plans`, and `terms`. The Strapi Public role has only `readForm`, `readPlans`, and `readTerms` under `api::quote-content.quote-content`. The static host proxies these three reads. The public frontend uses no API token.
- Never add duplicate field keys, option keys or semantic purposes. Field order is numeric, then stable field key on ties. Date of birth with the 18-year rule and vehicle year with its range rule are required for a usable form.
- Enter a rule argument or field default in the Strapi JSON editor as an object with a single `value` property, for example `{"value": 18}`, `{"value": false}` or `{"value": "2020-01-01"}`. Leave it empty for argument-free rules or fields with no default. Required selects start unselected and cannot have defaults. Present but invalid content leaves the whole form unavailable with a retry action.
- The version 1 decoder accepts up to 40 fields, 60 options per select, 12 rules per field and 240 UTF-16 units per content string. Text values allow up to 256 Unicode code points. Patterns are whole-value checks limited to 120 pattern units, literal characters, character classes and bounded counts through 24. The matcher uses a bounded set of offsets.
- Each country catalog may include up to 40 active published plans with up to 20 entries per coverage or benefit list. Plans sort by numeric order, then stable document ID. A malformed active published plan makes the country's catalog unavailable until the content is corrected.
- Each country has one published Terms document with a nonblank body of up to 20,000 UTF-16 code units. Missing, duplicate or invalid published terms block payment until recovered.
- Drafts and plan choices are isolated by URL country and retained in the current tab's `sessionStorage`, with a memory fallback if storage is unavailable. Reload revalidates against fresh published configuration. Quote data is excluded from API payloads, shareable URLs, and server persistence. SQLite holds Strapi content and its administrative metadata.
- Frontend SVGs are individual assets from Tabler Icons v3.41.1, tinted for the approved design. The Strapi favicon derives from the same shield. See the [MIT license](frontend/public/icons/TABLER-LICENSE.txt).
import type { FieldDefinition, FieldValue, FormDefinition, QuoteDraft } from '@quote/contract';

function maskDocument(value: string): string {
  const alphanumeric = /[\p{L}\p{N}]/u;
  const characters = [...value];
  const count = characters.filter((character) => alphanumeric.test(character)).length;
  if (!count) return '•'.repeat(characters.length);
  const visible = count > 4 ? 4 : count > 1 ? 1 : 0;
  let hidden = count - visible;
  return characters
    .map((character) => (alphanumeric.test(character) && hidden-- > 0 ? '•' : character))
    .join('');
}

function displayValue(field: FieldDefinition, value: FieldValue): string {
  if (field.purpose === 'identityDocument') return maskDocument(String(value));
  if (field.kind === 'select') return field.options.find(({ id }) => id === value)?.label ?? '';
  if (field.kind === 'checkbox') return value ? 'Sí' : 'No';
  if (field.kind === 'date') return String(value).split('-').reverse().join('/');
  return String(value);
}

export function reviewRows(form: FormDefinition, draft: QuoteDraft) {
  return form.fields.flatMap((field) => {
    const value = draft[field.id]?.value;
    return value == null || value === ''
      ? []
      : [{ id: field.id, label: field.label, value: displayValue(field, value) }];
  });
}

# US-03 — Summary and payment

**Status:** Draft 2 · Approved by the project owner on 2026-11-22

**Source:** [Technical assessment](../requirements/technical-assessment.pdf), pages 2–3 and 8–9

**Related story:** US-03 — Summary and payment

**Dependencies:** [US-01](US-01.md), [US-02](US-02.md), [ADR-001](../docs/adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md), [ADR-002](../docs/adr/ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md), [ADR-003](../docs/adr/ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md) and [ADR-004](../docs/adr/ADR-004-plan-catalog-and-selection.md)

## Objective

As a person who chose a plan, I want to review my quote and complete a simulated payment so that I can see confirmation of the quote.

US-03 consumes the active country's current, validated Details data and the explicitly selected plan with its final price. It adds the country-specific Strapi terms, consent and simulated payment result to the existing quote flow.

## Scope and dependencies

### In scope

- Show the current entered policyholder and vehicle values with their configured labels, plus the selected plan and its final price.
- Partially mask the identity document in the summary using the same rule in both countries, including its accessible presentation.
- Read the terms configured in Strapi for the active country. Before each Pay action, refresh the terms. Require acceptance of the terms currently presented and bind acceptance to their revision and the current quote snapshot.
- Allow a person to return to edit Details or change the plan within the same country. Retain valid saved values and selection under the approved US-01 and US-02 rules.
- Simulate successful and rejected payment outcomes using fictitious quote data only. A demo-only accessible outcome selector defaults to Approved and can select Rejected deterministically. Use one Pay action, block duplicate submissions while processing, and show one simulated quote number for a successful quote.
- On simulated failure, show a clear error and allow retry with the quote information retained.
- After reload, make an interrupted simulation retryable. Preserve a completed receipt and block another payment for the completed quote.
- Provide recoverable terms loading or retrieval failure states, keyboard operation, accessible labels/status, and usable mobile and desktop layouts.

### Dependencies on US-01 and US-02

- Summary requires valid current Details data for the country in the URL and a current, explicitly chosen eligible plan. Direct or history navigation cannot bypass these prerequisites. Reuse the US-02 fresh catalog validation before exposing Summary.
- The selected plan's configured base price is its final price under the approved US-02 decision. Use the country currency and formatting already defined there.
- Use each current form field's configured label and stable purpose metadata. Locate the document by `identityDocument` purpose, not by its label. Exclude values removed from the current form configuration.
- Same-country Back navigation retains the Details draft and plan candidate according to ADR-003 and ADR-004. Editing a field invalidates consent for the prior quote snapshot. The plan remains selected only under US-02's eligibility and price revalidation rule.

### Out of scope

- Real payment gateways, card collection, underwriting, quote persistence on a server, or cross-device payment deduplication.
- Changing the approved country boundary, form contract, plan contract, or final-price rule.
- Any new visual direction. Use the approved design system and existing wizard conventions when this story reaches design or implementation.

## Source requirements

| ID | Assessment requirement | Source |
|---|---|---|
| US03-SR-01 | Step 3 summarizes entered data and the chosen plan and offers payment. | Page 2, functional screen table |
| US03-SR-02 | Show policyholder data, vehicle data, chosen plan and final price. | Page 8, business rules |
| US03-SR-03 | Partially mask the document number in the summary. | Page 8, business rules |
| US03-SR-04 | Terms text varies by country and is managed by the business team in Strapi. | Page 8, context |
| US03-SR-05 | Return from summary to edit data or change the plan. | Page 8, business rules |
| US03-SR-06 | Payment is unavailable until terms are accepted. | Page 8, business rules and “Terms by country” scenario |
| US03-SR-07 | Payment cannot be submitted twice; successful payment shows a simulated quote number. | Page 8, business rules and “Successful payment” scenario |
| US03-SR-08 | A rejected simulated payment shows an error and can be retried without losing information. | Pages 8–9, “Rejected payment” scenario |
| US03-SR-09 | Use fictitious data only and no real payment integration. | Page 2, scope rules |
| US03-SR-10 | The wizard supports keyboard operation, accessible labels and mobile and desktop layouts. | Page 3, accessibility and responsive requirements |

## Functional acceptance criteria

### AC-US03-01 — Current quote summary

**Given** valid Details data and a currently eligible plan are present for the country in the URL

**When** the person reaches Summary

**Then** the summary shows entered policyholder and vehicle values using the current configured labels

**And** it shows the explicitly selected plan and its final price in that country's currency

**And** it excludes values discarded from the current form configuration

**And** it does not expose data from another country's quote.

### AC-US03-02 — Shared document masking rule

**Given** the current form has a field with `identityDocument` purpose and it has a value

**When** the summary is displayed or its accessible content is read

**Then** the same masking rule applies in Colombia and Chile, revealing at most the last four alphanumeric characters for longer values

**And** for values with two to four alphanumeric characters only the final character is revealed, with separators preserved

**And** a one-character value is fully masked

**And** its complete value is not exposed in the summary's visible or accessible presentation.

### AC-US03-03 — Country terms and consent

**Given** the person reaches Summary for Colombia or Chile

**When** the terms are loaded

**Then** the displayed text is the Strapi terms returned for that country

**And** payment is unavailable until the person accepts the displayed terms

**And** acceptance applies only to that terms revision and the current quote snapshot

**And** before each eligible Pay attempt, the app refreshes the terms from Strapi for the active country

**And** if that read returns the accepted revision and the quote snapshot is unchanged, payment may proceed

**And** if the read returns a changed revision, the updated text is presented and payment is blocked until the person reviews and accepts the new terms for the current quote snapshot.

### AC-US03-04 — Edit and change plan

**Given** the person is reviewing a quote

**When** they return to Details or Plans

**Then** they return within the same country

**And** the saved Details and eligible plan selection are retained according to US-01 and US-02 rules

**And** after any change, Summary uses the current validated values and current eligible plan price

**And** consent for a previous quote snapshot is not reused.

### AC-US03-05 — Successful simulated payment

**Given** the terms refresh returned the accepted revision and consent is current for the quote snapshot

**When** the person uses the single Pay action with the demo-only outcome set to Approved

# ADR-002 — Typed dynamic form contract and reconciliation

**Status** Human approved on 2026-11-22 ([approval record](../approvals/US-01-architecture-approval.md))  
**Applies to** US-01, with stable fields and roles for US-02 and US-03  
**Basis** [US-01 Draft 3](../../spec/US-01.md), especially AC-US01-02–04, 07–10 and 12–16, and [ADR-001](ADR-001-multi-country-content.md)

## Context

Strapi editors need to change field content and validation without rebuilding Angular. The application must reject a bad configuration atomically, preserve a compatible draft across changes, and display one configured error per field. A dynamic CMS key cannot provide static knowledge of its eventual widget or value type.

## Proposed decision

### Contract and failure behavior

Decode `unknown` once at each trust boundary using framework-independent TypeScript guards that produce a discriminated `FieldDefinition` union. A small shared workspace contract can supply the decoder, pure validation and fixtures to Strapi's projection and Angular's consumer. It carries no Angular or Strapi dependency and no customer data. Keep Strapi's nested editor representation behind its explicit projection. Contract version 1 is a fixed envelope with an exact version, the requested canonical country, and a nonempty fields array. Render content strings as text, including labels, help and errors. Each field has the following projected properties.

| Property | Version 1 proposal |
| --- | --- |
| `id`, `label`, `helpText`, `errorMessage` | Stable editor-maintained ID unique within the country form, Spanish label and fallback field error, and a required help-text property that permits an empty string. IDs are restricted opaque strings, protected from reserved object keys and independent of labels, order, and Strapi component IDs. |
| `kind`, `required`, `order` | One supported kind, a Boolean required flag, and a nonnegative safe-integer order. Sort by order, then by ID on a tie. Country is inherited from the form. |
| `rules` | Ordered array, possibly empty. Each rule specifies a recognized operator, its typed arguments when relevant, and its configured Spanish message. Order is the editor's array order. |
| `options`, `defaultValue` | Options are permitted only on selects and require stable unique option IDs and nonempty labels within each select. An omitted default means unset. A present default must meet the field's representation, available options, and configured rules. Fresh required selects start unset, so publishing a default for one is invalid. |
| `purpose` | Optional semantic marker, unique per reserved role. A usable form contains one required `dateOfBirth` date with `minimumAge` 18 and one required `vehicleYear` number with `vehicleYearRange`. `identityDocument` and `licensePlate` markers, when present, use text fields. This enables masking and pricing without relying on visible labels. |

Reject missing mandatory properties, missing published fields, date or number representation errors in rule arguments, incompatible defaults, unknown types or operators, duplicate IDs, and required selects with no valid options. Validate each option. An invalid option definition fails the snapshot. Allow an optional select to have no options and remain unset. Reject inverted range endpoints and a duplicate required rule. A rejected refresh never partially updates the view or the stored draft. Apply the error and retry behavior in ADR-001. Enforce size limits on fields, options, and text at the contract boundary. Choose exact limits during implementation against fixtures and document them.

### Type and rule compatibility

| Kinds and values | Supported operators |
| --- | --- |
| Text, a string, including document numbers and plates | `required`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern`, `email` |
| Number, a finite JavaScript number | `required`, `min`, `max`, `vehicleYearRange` for the vehicle-year purpose |
| Select, a listed stable option ID string | `required` |
| Date, a valid Gregorian ISO calendar-date string `YYYY-MM-DD` | `required`, `minDate`, `maxDate`, `minimumAge` for the date-of-birth purpose |
| Checkbox, a Boolean | `required`, which requires explicit `true` for a required checkbox |

- Keep a single required check. The field flag controls requiredness. An optional explicit `required` rule is valid only when the flag is true and supplies the required message. A required flag without the rule uses the field's configured error message. Required checks distinguish missing values from numeric zero. Whitespace-only text is empty for the required check and stored document or plate strings retain leading zeros. Non-required rules treat an unset value as inapplicable. An invalid typed entry is distinct from an unset value. Apply validators to every field and retain the ordered outcomes. The required error wins when present, then the first failing configured rule, then the field fallback for an invalid representation no configured rule describes.
- Length and age arguments are nonnegative integers, and lengths count Unicode code points. Numeric bounds are finite and inclusive. Vehicle year requires a safe integer and uses local browser Gregorian year Y with inclusive Y−20 through Y+1. Date bounds are valid ISO dates and inclusive. Calculate age using Gregorian calendar components and the browser's local civil date via an injectable clock, avoiding UTC parsing shifts. Propose March 1 for a February 29 birthday in non-leap years in the simulator. `required`, `email`, and `vehicleYearRange` take no argument.
- Treat patterns as declarative whole-value checks in a bounded safe subset. Propose bounded character classes, literal segments, and bounded repetitions, with no backreferences, lookaround, groups, or unbounded repetition. Cap both pattern and input lengths. Use a bounded non-backtracking matcher for the subset or equivalent implementation whose cost is bounded on rejected input. Validate editor patterns before the config reaches ready state. This makes formatting changes publishable while keeping pattern matching predictable.

### Angular form and accessibility

Use Typed Reactive Forms with `FormRecord<FormControl<FieldValue | null>>` and a discriminated field/view model. Keys are dynamic and the control's static value type is the common union. Narrow by the decoded field kind and normalize at the control adapter and output boundaries. Use actual typed number and Boolean values, preserve meaningful empty or unset state, and track rendered elements by stable ID. Stay with native inputs and selects and an unset, non-selectable required-select placeholder. The first invalid field gets focus on an unsuccessful Continue. Keep Continue available after the configuration is ready, with application validation controlling progress and custom messages. Use native form semantics with an explicit Angular submit handler and no browser validation bubbles masking configured messages. On blur expose that field's message, on change reevaluate touched fields, and on submit expose all applicable errors. Associate visible errors and help through stable DOM IDs and `aria-describedby`, and set `aria-invalid` when showing an error. Use concise status announcements for loading and retry, and avoid announcing the same validation error twice when moving focus. [Angular typed forms](https://angular.dev/guide/forms/typed-forms)

### Deterministic reconciliation

Rebuild the draft from the latest valid fields by ID instead of mutating the old key map in place. Omit removed or replaced IDs and obsolete select options entirely. For new IDs apply a valid allowed default or leave unset. For existing IDs preserve representable values and keep label, help, and order edits independent, even if updated business rules make a preserved value invalid. This lets users correct a value after a stricter constraint is published. Check the previous kind as well as the primitive value. Preserve a date as text, or text as a date only when it is already a valid ISO date. Clear other kind changes without implicit coercion. Select values require membership in the new option IDs and never migrate by label. Revalidate every field against the current clock and refreshed rules, write the clean snapshot atomically, and gate progression on the result. A restored valid required select stays selected. A fresh one, or one with an obsolete selection, shows its placeholder.

## Alternatives and consequences

| Alternative | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| Hardcoded Angular fields or a FormGroup with fixed keys | Strong static key typing, with a code change for each CMS field change. |
| Untyped forms or a general JSON Schema rendering engine | Simpler generalization, with weaker app-level typing or an extra dependency and a harder-to-explain CMS contract. |
| Signal Forms | Fits a signal-first model and is stable in Angular 22. The proposed Angular 21 baseline and requested form preference favor Typed Reactive Forms. Signals still own non-control state. |
| Directly execute CMS regexes or arbitrary editor rules | Broader flexibility, with less predictable runtime cost and harder validation of whole snapshots. |

The proposal makes unsupported widgets and rule language changes schema work. It protects the required age and year invariants while permitting published changes to supported field content. The type matrix, safe pattern subset, date boundary convention, and required-select default restriction are proposed architecture decisions. Verify DTO acceptance and rejection in both consumers, age and year boundaries, required-first and rule order, data reconciliation, stale response rejection, keyboard focus, and the two required-select states. See T-US01-02–06, 08–10, 12 and 14–16. The final quote-summary view remains under US-03.
# ADR-003 — Frontend-only wizard state

**Status** Human approved on 2026-11-22 ([approval record](../approvals/US-01-architecture-approval.md))  
**Applies to** US-01, with shared state boundaries for US-02 and US-03  
**Basis** [US-01 Draft 3](../../spec/US-01.md), assessment pp. 2 and 6–9, and project owner's frontend-only data boundary

## Context

Step 1 must restore a draft when navigating back and reconcile from a newly retrieved form. Later steps depend on the same vehicle and policyholder data, plan selection, and terms and simulated payment status. Strapi owns business content. It does not receive customer, vehicle, quote, plan selection, or payment data.

## Proposed decision

Use a small Angular Signals store with explicit commands, typed snapshots, and read-only projections. Scope it to the app's quoting flow so route components can be recreated. Pass the country's decoded Router value to state accessors and store separate country snapshots. Never read a previous country's data while a new country is loading. Store normalized typed drafts with original field kind and stable field identifier; keep touch/submit and focus state in the component. The reconciler atomically replaces the active snapshot after a valid refresh and the store supplies the later-step projection only for the active country.

Use a small versioned, tab-scoped `sessionStorage` envelope for fictitious wizard state. The signal store owns the current state; the adapter writes full snapshots and validates the restored shape and country. Treat browser storage as untrusted, revalidate fields against freshly retrieved content before advancing, and reject malformed or unknown-version stored data. A recoverable content error retains the draft but blocks progression. If storage is blocked or fails, continue using memory for the current page session and make reload recovery unavailable. Clear the country draft when the user starts a new quote. Do not put quote data in URLs, cookies, analytics, diagnostic logs, content requests, or server persistence. App-opened separate tabs should omit `opener` where relevant. A duplicated or opener-linked tab can inherit an initial copy and then diverge. The design promises no cross-tab or cross-device guarantees. [HTML Web Storage standard](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html)

The US-01 step-2 handoff can be verified with a same-country route or narrow screen that allows going back. It owns no plan UI or plan business behavior. Future deep links to plans or summary check the matching country and current prerequisites, then navigate to the earliest incomplete step within that country. Client guards are wizard navigation controls. The data boundary is implemented by the public API shape and the absence of quote-write operations. [Angular Router guards](https://angular.dev/guide/routing/route-guards)

## Consequences for later stories

- **US-02** consumes a current, validated Step 1 snapshot and published active country plans. Store only one selected plan reference per quote along with the calculated price snapshot and its inputs or revision linkage as specified later. A change to inputs or available plans invalidates dependent selections or totals when the later rules require it. Recheck prerequisites before summary.
- **US-03** derives the review from current country fields and masks the identity document in presentation. Use stable field purpose metadata to locate the document independently of its label. Bind consent to the current terms revision and quote snapshot. Proposed duplicate protection is an atomic attempt transition in the same store, from eligible to processing before the asynchronous simulation starts. Only the matching attempt can settle, repeat clicks do not enqueue, success keeps one confirmation number for that completed quote, and a reported failure may retry. The US-03 spec and checkpoint will decide how reload handles a persisted processing attempt and completed receipt. No real gateway, card data or global idempotency service is implied.

## Alternatives and consequences

| Alternative | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| Memory only | Lowest retention, with loss on reload and no reconciliation of previously saved data after refresh. |
| Browser persistent storage or IndexedDB | Longer recovery and broader synchronization options, with unnecessary fictitious customer-data retention and more cleanup or coordination. |
| Server quote collection or hosted state | Could support cross-device resume and global deduplication, contrary to the frontend-only customer and quote data boundary. |
| General-purpose state management library | Provides conventions for large applications. Three wizard steps can share a signal store without that dependency. |

Verify same-country Back and Forward, country-switch isolation, restoration plus reconciliation after reload, graceful storage failure, and exclusion of quote data from network requests. Exercise duplicate payment attempts and reload outcomes under US-03. US-01 traces to AC-US01-06, 08, 09, 13 and 14 and T-US01-07, 08, 09, 13 and 14.

[Angular Signals](https://angular.dev/guide/signals)
# ADR-005 — Published terms and simulated payment

**Status** Human approved on 2026-11-22 ([approval record](../approvals/US-03-architecture-approval.md))

**Applies to** US-03

**Basis** [Approved US-03 Draft 2](../../spec/US-03.md), [specification approval](../approvals/US-03-spec-approval.md), assessment pp. 2 and 8–9

## Context

[ADR-001](ADR-001-multi-country-content.md) reserves a country-scoped terms document and public read action. [ADR-002](ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md) establishes the shared runtime decoder pattern. [ADR-003](ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md) keeps quote state and payment in the browser, and [ADR-004](ADR-004-plan-catalog-and-selection.md) already gates editable Summary on valid Details and a freshly revalidated plan. The existing Angular 21.2 wizard has the Summary handoff and the Strapi 5.63 controller already serves Form and Plans through the same-origin proxy. US-03 needs a terms revision contract, a payment attempt that refreshes consent before it starts, and a terminal receipt that survives reload.

## Proposed decision

### Published terms contract

Create a Terms collection with Draft & Publish and one document per country. Use the existing country enum and a required, nonblank multiline plain-text body of at most 20,000 UTF-16 code units. Preserve the body as returned by Strapi, including paragraph breaks. Read only the published country document through the Document Service, selecting only country and body. Read up to two documents to detect duplicate publications and fail if either the country or body is invalid. Seed one fictitious, country-specific publication for Colombia and Chile in the existing startup workflow. Track seeding separately from Forms and Plans, skip countries with existing Terms documents during initial seeding, and preserve editorial changes and deliberate unpublication on subsequent starts. [Strapi publication status](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/document-service/status)

Add `GET /api/quote-content/v1/:country/terms` to the existing quote-content controller. Use the existing country parser and reject request query parameters. Project `{ schemaVersion: 1, country, revision, text }`. Define `revision` as the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the UTF-8 JSON tuple `[1, country, text]`, computed by Strapi from the projected values. It identifies the exact country text the user can accept. Publishing changed text changes its revision and republishing identical text keeps the revision. The shared `@quote/contract` decoder checks the envelope version, expected country, revision format and text bounds at the server and browser boundaries. Angular presents terms as text, preserving line breaks and treating markup as literal content. [Angular security](https://angular.dev/best-practices/security)

| Outcome | Response |
| --- | --- |
| Valid published document | `200` with the terms envelope |
| Unexpected query parameters or unsupported country | `400 INVALID_REQUEST` or `404 UNSUPPORTED_COUNTRY`, respectively |
| No published document | `404 TERMS_NOT_PUBLISHED` |
| Duplicate or invalid published configuration | `503 TERMS_UNAVAILABLE` |
| CMS retrieval failure | `503 CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE` |

Reuse the `{ error: { code } }` envelope and `Cache-Control: no-store` on handler outcomes. Extend the same-origin, GET-only proxy allowlist and add only `api::quote-content.quote-content.readTerms` to the Public role alongside Form and Plans. Generated CRUD, draft and admin access, and write credentials stay outside the public contract. The terms request carries the country in the path and no quote, consent or payment data. The proxy bypasses caching as it does for Form and Plans. [HTTP caching](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111.html)

### Summary and consent

Extend the existing Summary handoff. Build a read-only review projection from the active country's validated, reconciled Details and freshly selected Plan. Use current field order, labels and option labels, the existing money formatter and the plan's final price. Mask the `identityDocument` value before it enters the review projection so both visible and accessible output use the same masked string. Apply Q-US03-01 to alphanumeric characters, preserving separators. Keep the raw value in the existing Details draft only. There is no additional form field or network contract for the review.

Read Terms on Summary entry and explicit retry through the existing `HttpClient` and signals pattern. Bind consent in memory to the active country, terms revision and the review snapshot. Compare snapshots by value using the current field identifiers, kinds and normalized values, and the selected plan ID and final money value. Navigation back to edit preserves Details and the plan candidate under their existing rules. A change to normalized quote data, plan, price or terms revision invalidates consent. Cancellation and generation checks prevent superseded responses from replacing active terms. Loading or failed reads leave the review available with payment blocked. A successful recovery read may restore eligibility using prior consent only if the revision, text and quote snapshot still match. Recovery itself never invokes the simulator. The next Pay still performs its own fresh read. [Angular HTTP requests](https://angular.dev/guide/http/making-requests)

### One simulated attempt and terminal recovery

1. The quote feature owns one attempt state per country. A single Pay command checks the live editable Summary prerequisites, consent and absence of a busy or completed payment. It synchronously reserves an attempt before requesting fresh country Terms. That reservation locks submission during both the refresh and the simulation. The attempt captures the country, active Summary generation, consent binding and the selected demo outcome.
2. Only the current attempt may act on the refresh result. Recheck the active country and Summary generation, current Details and plan validity, quote snapshot, and consent. A valid changed revision replaces the presented terms and clears consent. A failed or invalid read leaves a recoverable terms error. These outcomes release the reservation without invoking the simulator. If the quote or consent changed during the read, release the reservation and let the existing prerequisite checks run. A match on revision, terms text and quote snapshot advances directly to processing under the same reservation. A response that pairs the accepted revision with different text is invalid.
3. The local asynchronous simulator accepts only the captured Approved or Rejected outcome. Approved is the selector default. Outcome changes after reservation apply to a subsequent attempt. The simulator has no external side effects and takes no card, Details or plan data. Only the matching live attempt may settle. Rejection releases the lock with a retryable error and keeps the draft, selected plan and matching consent. A retry goes through the same Pay command and a fresh terms read. Leaving Summary, switching country or replacing the quote invalidates outstanding work. Cancel pending reads and ignore callbacks that can no longer settle. Browser Back or Forward cannot replay Pay.
4. Success creates one browser-generated opaque simulated quote number and commits an immutable terminal receipt once. Persist only the minimal completed receipt in a bounded, versioned country-scoped `sessionStorage` record alongside the existing draft and plan entries. Keep country and quote number in the receipt. Decode the record as untrusted input, rejecting oversized, unknown-version, malformed or wrong-country values. Consent and unfinished attempts stay in memory. After reload, an interrupted attempt therefore cannot resume or settle. The person returns through the existing Details and plan checks and can retry after current consent. If storage is unavailable, retain the same duplicate guard and receipt for the current page session under ADR-003. [HTML Web Storage](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html)
5. A valid restored receipt is the terminal confirmation for the current country quote. On the Summary route, restore that confirmation without opening editable Summary or presenting live plan, price or terms as part of the receipt. CMS changes and edits reached through browser history cannot alter or reopen a settled result. Switching back to that country preserves the receipt. ADR-003 reserves clearing the country quote for an explicit start-new-quote reset. The current app has no such action, and US-03 requires only the reset boundary. A future explicit reset clears the receipt, draft, plan and in-memory payment state, with the terminal lock cleared last so a partial reset cannot silently reopen the completed quote. Editable Summary for an unfinished or explicitly reset quote still uses the live prerequisite redirects in ADR-004.

## Alternatives and consequences

| Alternative | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| Embed Terms in Form Configuration or expose generated Strapi reads | Embedding ties independent publication schedules together. Generated reads widen the public surface. The dedicated action adds one bounded response and Public permission. |
| Use `updatedAt`, `publishedAt` or an editor-entered revision | Metadata can change while the displayed text is unchanged. Manual revisions can drift from text. The content fingerprint follows what the person reviews and accepts. |
| Trust terms from Summary entry or lock only once simulation begins | Entry-only terms can miss a published change. A later lock allows overlapping Pay refreshes. Reserving before the fresh read costs one terms request per eligible Pay attempt and closes that overlap. A CMS publication after the successful read may still occur while the local simulation runs. |
| Persist consent and unfinished attempts or require fresh CMS data to restore a receipt | Persisting in-flight state needs restoration rules and risks replay. Revalidating a historical receipt against current editorial data can erase access to a completed result. A minimal terminal record supports reload without reviving unfinished work or copying quote details. |
| Add a server-side payment endpoint | Server persistence could coordinate across tabs or devices. The approved simulator is local, so tab-scoped duplicate protection has no server or gateway dependency. |

# ADR-005 amendment — Terminal quote and restart

**Status** Human approved on 2026-11-22 ([approval record](../approvals/US-03-terminal-quote-architecture-approval.md))

**Applies to** US-03, AC-US03-R01 through AC-US03-R04

**Basis** [Approved terminal quote revision](../../spec/US-03-terminal-quote-revision.md), [revision approval](../approvals/US-03-terminal-quote-spec-approval.md) and [ADR-005](ADR-005-country-terms-and-simulated-payment.md)

## Context

The approved revision changes the completed quote behavior in steps 4 and 5 of ADR-005. The existing Angular wizard reads a minimal receipt on Summary, but can still open editable Details and Plans with that receipt present. It stores editable Details, the plan candidate and the receipt in independent country-scoped keys. The revision makes confirmation terminal across wizard routes, restores the captured review and introduces an explicit country-scoped restart. The content and payment boundaries in [ADR-001](ADR-001-multi-country-content.md), [ADR-003](ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md), [ADR-004](ADR-004-plan-catalog-and-selection.md) and ADR-005 continue to apply to unfinished quotes.

## Proposed decisions

### Gate the wizard on the terminal receipt

Keep `/:country/quote/summary` as the confirmation route for a completed quote. Continue using the existing route parameter subscription, including for a reused quote component and browser history. Decode the country and synchronously resolve its terminal receipt before exposing any editable route state or requesting live quote content. A valid receipt takes precedence over Details, Plans and editable Summary. Replace an attempted same-country Details or Plans history entry with the canonical Summary URL and render only confirmation. No editable control is instantiated while the redirect is pending. Confirmation reads the receipt directly and has no form, catalog or terms prerequisite. Keep the terminal check reactive so successful completion also switches the current Summary to confirmation without waiting for a navigation. [Angular route state](https://angular.dev/guide/routing/read-route-state) · [Angular Signals](https://angular.dev/guide/signals)

Reuse the route and attempt generations to suppress superseded work at navigation and restart. A retained event or delayed response must not re-enter an editable step, persist an old draft or plan, or settle an attempt after the quote becomes terminal or its state is reset. Receipt lookup and redirect decisions always use the canonical active country. Rejection creates no receipt and keeps the existing edit, plan selection and retry behavior, including a fresh terms check on Pay.

### Freeze the review at approval

After the live attempt passes its final eligibility check, use the existing review projector to capture ordered label and display-value rows, including the already masked identity document. Capture the chosen plan's displayed name and validated final `{ amountMinor, currency }` at the same transition. Generate the existing opaque quote reference once and commit the immutable receipt as one snapshot. Copy display values out of the editable state. Restore and display the snapshot with the existing country money formatter. A published change, removal or outage cannot alter it. Treat values as plain text in both visible and accessible output.

Store `{ version: 2, country, number, review: { rows, planName, price } }` in the existing per-country receipt key, `quote-receipt-v1:<country>`. The key stays stable. The envelope version determines the decoder. Persist only row id, display label and display value for each row, alongside the plan name and typed price. Keep the raw document, full draft, full plan catalog, terms, consent and attempt data out of the receipt.

Validate one bounded envelope before rendering. Check version, country, quote reference format, ordered rows with unique valid field ids, text limits and country money. Use the existing form and plan contract limits as the source for bounds. The current contract permits 40 rows, field ids of up to 40 safe characters, labels and plan names of up to 240 UTF-16 code units, and free text of up to 256 Unicode code points. A projected value therefore needs up to 512 UTF-16 code units, including supplementary characters. The field and string limits plus worst-case JSON escaping, price and envelope fit within a 200,000 UTF-16 code unit pre-parse limit. Use only the decoded fields for rendering. An invalid version 2 record does not fall back to a reference-only receipt. If writing a valid receipt fails, preserve the full terminal receipt and duplicate lock in memory under ADR-003 and surface that reload recovery is unavailable. Never write a partial or version 1 substitute.

Continue decoding the existing version 1 envelope in that same key with its original bounds and country and number checks. It restores the original reference, terminal gate and restart behavior. Its historical review is unavailable. There is no backfill from mutable state and no migration write during restore. The single key avoids a second legacy lookup that could revive an old receipt after restart.

### Restart and release the terminal lock last

Use one restart command for the active country and terminal receipt. Run the synchronous persistence sequence through the existing state owners, with an explicit outcome for every storage action. The current draft and candidate persistence helpers can swallow failures for ordinary edits. Restart must observe failures and may not use silent success from those paths. [HTML Web Storage](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html)

1. Keep confirmation and the terminal guard in place throughout reset. Invalidate pending country-scoped form, plan, terms and payment work before clearing persisted state. Ignore repeated reset requests while a reset is in progress.
2. Remove the active country's draft and candidate keys and read each back to confirm absence. A failure stops the reset before touching the receipt key. A partially cleared draft or candidate stays inaccessible behind the receipt. Retry repeats the removals safely. The other country is outside this operation.
3. After both absence checks succeed, remove the active country's single receipt key. This is the persistent commit point for both version 1 and version 2. A thrown removal leaves the terminal receipt and lock in place. A successful Web Storage removal commits the durable reset. Avoid a further fallible storage read or write between that deletion and clearing memory. There is no secondary receipt key to delete or fall back to.
4. Clear that country's in-memory draft, plan candidate, terms and consent, and attempt and receipt state. Use explicit empty memory state so restoration cannot re-read old objects. Release the in-memory terminal lock last and navigate to canonical same-country Details with fresh configuration and its defaults. Failure to load configuration or complete navigation after the reset uses the wizard's existing recovery paths. It does not revert the reset. Old Summary history entries go through unfinished-quote prerequisites.

If storage cannot be accessed or a required cleanup cannot be verified before the commit point, report a retryable restart failure and stay terminal. A memory-only receipt can restart after the same cleanup succeeds, including when its receipt key was never written. The pre-existing memory fallback still limits reload guarantees when storage was unavailable during approval.

## Alternatives and consequences

| Alternative | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| Gate only Summary or restore by replaying live reads | An editable route could reopen the flow, and historical values could change with publication or retrieval failures. The route gate and stored review remove both dependencies. |
| Store a raw draft and full plan DTO in the receipt | Reformatting would depend on future schemas and expose more editable data to receipt storage. The bounded display snapshot preserves the approved view with less data. |
| Add a separate version 2 receipt key or migrate all quote state into one envelope | Both require coordinating old and new keys during restore and reset. Versioning the existing receipt envelope lets one final removal clear either format. |
| Clear memory first or delete the receipt before the draft and plan | A failure could reopen a quote with stale data or leave a receipt that returns on reload. The terminal record remains until earlier cleanup is verified. |

## Verification

- **AC-US03-R01** — In CO and CL, verify a completed quote reaches only confirmation through direct URLs, Back, Forward and reload, and edits cannot briefly render. Check legacy receipts and navigation to the other country.
- **AC-US03-R02** — In each country, compare the masked captured review, amount and reference after changed or unavailable Strapi content. Test the worst-case valid projection against the codec, and reject corrupted and wrong-country envelopes. Verify that failed writes retain the full review in memory.
- **AC-US03-R03** — Verify reset of both receipt versions, fresh Details defaults and absence of the old approval after reload and history navigation. Inject failure at each durable cleanup stage, check that reload stays terminal with the existing stored receipt, and verify a retry can complete. Verify no changes to the other country.
- **AC-US03-R04** — In both countries, verify rejection retains the draft and plan candidate, allows edit routes, and retries using the existing consent and fresh-terms rules.

# US-03 — Summary and payment

**Status:** Draft 2 · Approved by the project owner on 2026-11-22

**Source:** [Technical assessment](../requirements/technical-assessment.pdf), pages 2–3 and 8–9

**Related story:** US-03 — Summary and payment

**Dependencies:** [US-01](US-01.md), [US-02](US-02.md), [ADR-001](../docs/adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md), [ADR-002](../docs/adr/ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md), [ADR-003](../docs/adr/ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md) and [ADR-004](../docs/adr/ADR-004-plan-catalog-and-selection.md)

## Objective

As a person who chose a plan, I want to review my quote and complete a simulated payment so that I can see confirmation of the quote.

US-03 consumes the active country's current, validated Details data and the explicitly selected plan with its final price. It adds the country-specific Strapi terms, consent and simulated payment result to the existing quote flow.

## Scope and dependencies

### In scope

- Show the current entered policyholder and vehicle values with their configured labels, plus the selected plan and its final price.
- Partially mask the identity document in the summary using the same rule in both countries, including its accessible presentation.
- Read the terms configured in Strapi for the active country. Before each Pay action, refresh the terms. Require acceptance of the terms currently presented and bind acceptance to their revision and the current quote snapshot.
- Allow a person to return to edit Details or change the plan within the same country. Retain valid saved values and selection under the approved US-01 and US-02 rules.
- Simulate successful and rejected payment outcomes using fictitious quote data only. A demo-only accessible outcome selector defaults to Approved and can select Rejected deterministically. Use one Pay action, block duplicate submissions while processing, and show one simulated quote number for a successful quote.
- On simulated failure, show a clear error and allow retry with the quote information retained.
- After reload, make an interrupted simulation retryable. Preserve a completed receipt and block another payment for the completed quote.
- Provide recoverable terms loading or retrieval failure states, keyboard operation, accessible labels/status, and usable mobile and desktop layouts.

### Dependencies on US-01 and US-02

- Summary requires valid current Details data for the country in the URL and a current, explicitly chosen eligible plan. Direct or history navigation cannot bypass these prerequisites. Reuse the US-02 fresh catalog validation before exposing Summary.
- The selected plan's configured base price is its final price under the approved US-02 decision. Use the country currency and formatting already defined there.
- Use each current form field's configured label and stable purpose metadata. Locate the document by `identityDocument` purpose, not by its label. Exclude values removed from the current form configuration.
- Same-country Back navigation retains the Details draft and plan candidate according to ADR-003 and ADR-004. Editing a field invalidates consent for the prior quote snapshot. The plan remains selected only under US-02's eligibility and price revalidation rule.

### Out of scope

- Real payment gateways, card collection, underwriting, quote persistence on a server, or cross-device payment deduplication.
- Changing the approved country boundary, form contract, plan contract, or final-price rule.
- Any new visual direction. Use the approved design system and existing wizard conventions when this story reaches design or implementation.

## Source requirements

| ID | Assessment requirement | Source |
|---|---|---|
| US03-SR-01 | Step 3 summarizes entered data and the chosen plan and offers payment. | Page 2, functional screen table |
| US03-SR-02 | Show policyholder data, vehicle data, chosen plan and final price. | Page 8, business rules |
| US03-SR-03 | Partially mask the document number in the summary. | Page 8, business rules |
| US03-SR-04 | Terms text varies by country and is managed by the business team in Strapi. | Page 8, context |
| US03-SR-05 | Return from summary to edit data or change the plan. | Page 8, business rules |
| US03-SR-06 | Payment is unavailable until terms are accepted. | Page 8, business rules and “Terms by country” scenario |
| US03-SR-07 | Payment cannot be submitted twice; successful payment shows a simulated quote number. | Page 8, business rules and “Successful payment” scenario |
| US03-SR-08 | A rejected simulated payment shows an error and can be retried without losing information. | Pages 8–9, “Rejected payment” scenario |
| US03-SR-09 | Use fictitious data only and no real payment integration. | Page 2, scope rules |
| US03-SR-10 | The wizard supports keyboard operation, accessible labels and mobile and desktop layouts. | Page 3, accessibility and responsive requirements |

## Functional acceptance criteria

### AC-US03-01 — Current quote summary

**Given** valid Details data and a currently eligible plan are present for the country in the URL

**When** the person reaches Summary

**Then** the summary shows entered policyholder and vehicle values using the current configured labels

**And** it shows the explicitly selected plan and its final price in that country's currency

**And** it excludes values discarded from the current form configuration

**And** it does not expose data from another country's quote.

### AC-US03-02 — Shared document masking rule

**Given** the current form has a field with `identityDocument` purpose and it has a value

**When** the summary is displayed or its accessible content is read

**Then** the same masking rule applies in Colombia and Chile, revealing at most the last four alphanumeric characters for longer values

**And** for values with two to four alphanumeric characters only the final character is revealed, with separators preserved

**And** a one-character value is fully masked

**And** its complete value is not exposed in the summary's visible or accessible presentation.

### AC-US03-03 — Country terms and consent

**Given** the person reaches Summary for Colombia or Chile

**When** the terms are loaded

**Then** the displayed text is the Strapi terms returned for that country

**And** payment is unavailable until the person accepts the displayed terms

**And** acceptance applies only to that terms revision and the current quote snapshot

**And** before each eligible Pay attempt, the app refreshes the terms from Strapi for the active country

**And** if that read returns the accepted revision and the quote snapshot is unchanged, payment may proceed

**And** if the read returns a changed revision, the updated text is presented and payment is blocked until the person reviews and accepts the new terms for the current quote snapshot.

### AC-US03-04 — Edit and change plan

**Given** the person is reviewing a quote

**When** they return to Details or Plans

**Then** they return within the same country

**And** the saved Details and eligible plan selection are retained according to US-01 and US-02 rules

**And** after any change, Summary uses the current validated values and current eligible plan price

**And** consent for a previous quote snapshot is not reused.

### AC-US03-05 — Successful simulated payment

**Given** the terms refresh returned the accepted revision and consent is current for the quote snapshot

**When** the person uses the single Pay action with the demo-only outcome set to Approved

Generate the existing opaque quote reference once and commit the immutable receipt as one snapshot. Copy display values out of the editable state. Restore and display the snapshot with the existing country money formatter. A published change, removal or outage cannot alter it. Treat values as plain text in both visible and accessible output.

Store `{ version: 2, country, number, review: { rows, planName, price } }` in the existing per-country receipt key, `quote-receipt-v1:<country>`. The key stays stable. The envelope version determines the decoder. Persist only row id, display label and display value for each row, alongside the plan name and typed price. Keep the raw document, full draft, full plan catalog, terms, consent and attempt data out of the receipt.

Validate one bounded envelope before rendering. Check version, country, quote reference format, ordered rows with unique valid field ids, text limits and country money. Use the existing form and plan contract limits as the source for bounds. The current contract permits 40 rows, field ids of up to 40 safe characters, labels and plan names of up to 240 UTF-16 code units, and free text of up to 256 Unicode code points. A projected value therefore needs up to 512 UTF-16 code units, including supplementary characters. The field and string limits plus worst-case JSON escaping, price and envelope fit within a 200,000 UTF-16 code unit pre-parse limit. Use only the decoded fields for rendering. An invalid version 2 record does not fall back to a reference-only receipt. If writing a valid receipt fails, preserve the full terminal receipt and duplicate lock in memory under ADR-003 and surface that reload recovery is unavailable. Never write a partial or version 1 substitute.

Continue decoding the existing version 1 envelope in that same key with its original bounds and country and number checks. It restores the original reference, terminal gate and restart behavior. Its historical review is unavailable. There is no backfill from mutable state and no migration write during restore. The single key avoids a second legacy lookup that could revive an old receipt after restart.

### Restart and release the terminal lock last

Use one restart command for the active country and terminal receipt. Run the synchronous persistence sequence through the existing state owners, with an explicit outcome for every storage action. The current draft and candidate persistence helpers can swallow failures for ordinary edits. Restart must observe failures and may not use silent success from those paths. [HTML Web Storage](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html)

1. Keep confirmation and the terminal guard in place throughout reset. Invalidate pending country-scoped form, plan, terms and payment work before clearing persisted state. Ignore repeated reset requests while a reset is in progress.
2. Remove the active country's draft and candidate keys and read each back to confirm absence. A failure stops the reset before touching the receipt key. A partially cleared draft or candidate stays inaccessible behind the receipt. Retry repeats the removals safely. The other country is outside this operation.
3. After both absence checks succeed, remove the active country's single receipt key. This is the persistent commit point for both version 1 and version 2. A thrown removal leaves the terminal receipt and lock in place. A successful Web Storage removal commits the durable reset. Avoid a further fallible storage read or write between that deletion and clearing memory. There is no secondary receipt key to delete or fall back to.
4. Clear that country's in-memory draft, plan candidate, terms and consent, and attempt and receipt state. Use explicit empty memory state so restoration cannot re-read old objects. Release the in-memory terminal lock last and navigate to canonical same-country Details with fresh configuration and its defaults. Failure to load configuration or complete navigation after the reset uses the wizard's existing recovery paths. It does not revert the reset. Old Summary history entries go through unfinished-quote prerequisites.

If storage cannot be accessed or a required cleanup cannot be verified before the commit point, report a retryable restart failure and stay terminal. A memory-only receipt can restart after the same cleanup succeeds, including when its receipt key was never written. The pre-existing memory fallback still limits reload guarantees when storage was unavailable during approval.

## Alternatives and consequences

| Alternative | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| Gate only Summary or restore by replaying live reads | An editable route could reopen the flow, and historical values could change with publication or retrieval failures. The route gate and stored review remove both dependencies. |
| Store a raw draft and full plan DTO in the receipt | Reformatting would depend on future schemas and expose more editable data to receipt storage. The bounded display snapshot preserves the approved view with less data. |
| Add a separate version 2 receipt key or migrate all quote state into one envelope | Both require coordinating old and new keys during restore and reset. Versioning the existing receipt envelope lets one final removal clear either format. |
| Clear memory first or delete the receipt before the draft and plan | A failure could reopen a quote with stale data or leave a receipt that returns on reload. The terminal record remains until earlier cleanup is verified. |

- **AC-US03-R01** — In CO and CL, verify a completed quote reaches only confirmation through direct URLs, Back, Forward and reload, and edits cannot briefly render. Check legacy receipts and navigation to the other country.
- **AC-US03-R02** — In each country, compare the masked captured review, amount and reference after changed or unavailable Strapi content. Test the worst-case valid projection against the codec, and reject corrupted and wrong-country envelopes. Verify that failed writes retain the full review in memory.
- **AC-US03-R03** — Verify reset of both receipt versions, fresh Details defaults and absence of the old approval after reload and history navigation. Inject failure at each durable cleanup stage, check that reload stays terminal with the existing stored receipt, and verify a retry can complete. Verify no changes to the other country.
- **AC-US03-R04** — In both countries, verify rejection retains the draft and plan candidate, allows edit routes, and retries using the existing consent and fresh-terms rules.
